description: Block F-84F-30-RE; served the 7625th Operations Squadron at the USAF Academy then the 27th Strategic Fighter Wing at Bergstrom AFB then the 162nd Fighter Squadron 178th TFG Ohio ANG; to the NMUSAF loan programme circa October 1970 and loaned back to the 178th at Springfield; photographed on site 9 November 1980 and 23 May 2005; no sighting found later than 2012 so 2026 presence is unconfirmed
museum_name: Springfield-Beckley Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: Block F-84G-1-RE; taken on strength circa 1951 and released 15 September 1958 to Kent State University as civil N5582A with the registration cancelled 24 February 1964; to the NMUSAF loan programme and loaned June 1982 to the 178th Fighter Group at Springfield; photographed on site 23 May 2005; 2026 presence unconfirmed
museum_name: Springfield-Beckley Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: Construction number D-300; taken on strength 1973 with the 23rd Tactical Fighter Wing at England AFB Louisiana and the 76th TFS; to the 162nd TFS 178th TFG Ohio ANG at Springfield in 1977 or 1978; withdrawn from use June 1992 and placed as a gate guardian on the ANG side of the airport; an NMUSAF loan; photographed on site 23 May 2005; the reported name City of Springfield could not be verified in any source so aircraft_name is left blank; 2026 presence unconfirmed
aliases: A-7D-12-CV; Corsair II; c/n D-300; A7; A7D
museum_name: Springfield-Beckley Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: Construction number 192-54; accepted by the USAF 15 September 1954; 479th TFW at George AFB 1955; 3595th Combat Crew Training Wing at Nellis AFB 1956; 188th TFS New Mexico ANG 1958; 118th TFS Connecticut ANG 1964; to the USAF Museum at Patterson Field December 1964 and to the museum at Wright Field October 1970; loaned to the Ohio ANG 178th FG at Springfield June 1982; wears the shortened marking 53-559 on the fin; 2026 presence unconfirmed
museum_name: Springfield-Beckley Air National Guard Base Air Park
